data.description:
## What
Implement plugins/dso/scripts/inference-recall-replay.sh — the replay harness that processes incidents.jsonl through the inference-challenge system and measures recall/precision.

## Why
This is the core SC4 deliverable: in-session closure gate validating recall >=50% all / >=70% held-out and precision >=0.5.

## Implementation

### File: plugins/dso/scripts/inference-recall-replay.sh

### Interface
```
inference-recall-replay.sh \
  [--corpus=<path>]          # default: tests/fixtures/inference-incidents/incidents.jsonl
  [--holdout=<path>]         # default: tests/fixtures/inference-incidents/holdout.txt
  [--classifier-cmd=<cmd>]   # default: .claude/scripts/dso ticket ... (or stub path during dev)
  [--output=json|text]       # default: json
  [--dry-run]                # skip classifier invocation, use corpus affects_fields directly
```

### Algorithm
1. Load incidents.jsonl (one JSON object per line)
2. Corpus size check: if count < 10 → emit CORPUS_INSUFFICIENT, exit 1
3. Corpus quality check: for each incident, verify ticket_id via TICKET_EXISTS_CMD (default: .claude/scripts/dso ticket exists); exclude invalid incidents, emit CORPUS_QUALITY_WARNING to stderr if any excluded
4. After exclusion, re-check count: if < 10 → CORPUS_INSUFFICIENT
5. Load holdout.txt (one incident_id per line) to identify held-out partition
6. For each incident, invoke the affects_fields classifier on inferred_decision_text → determines whether INFERENCE_CHALLENGE would fire (high-stakes → 100% review; rationale-text-only → 20% deterministic via hash(decision_id) mod 5 == 0)
7. Compute: recalled_all = challenged_count / total; recalled_holdout = challenged_holdout / holdout_total; precision = real_incidents_in_challenged / total_challenged
8. Emit RECALL_RESULT JSON signal to stdout
9. Exit 0 if all thresholds met (recall_all>=0.5, recall_holdout>=0.7, precision>=0.5); exit 2 if any threshold fails

### Signal: RECALL_RESULT
```json
{
  "signal": "RECALL_RESULT",
  "recall_all": <float>,
  "recall_holdout": <float>,
  "precision": <float>,
  "corpus_size": <int>,
  "holdout_size": <int>,
  "all_passed": <bool>,
  "thresholds": {"recall_all": 0.5, "recall_holdout": 0.7, "precision": 0.5}
}
```

### Signal: CORPUS_INSUFFICIENT
```json
{"signal": "CORPUS_INSUFFICIENT", "corpus_size": <int>, "minimum_required": 10}
```

### Metric computation
Delegate float arithmetic to Python3 inline heredoc (avoids bc portability issues) or a companion inference-recall-metrics.py helper.

### Classifier integration
The harness invokes the affects_fields classifier via CLASSIFIER_CMD env var (default: the classifier shipped in S3 / 18b0-7c5d). During development (before S3 lands), CLASSIFIER_CMD can point to a stub that echoes affects_fields from the incident record itself. Final closure gate MUST use the production classifier.

### Constraints
- _PLUGIN_ROOT pattern for all paths (no hardcoded plugins/dso/)
- All temp files via mktemp
- Executable bit set (chmod +x)
- Reads TICKET_EXISTS_CMD env var with default fallback

## AC: all 3 RED test files pass after this implementation
data.title: GREEN: implement inference-recall-replay.sh harness with CORPUS_INSUFFICIENT guard, corpus quality check, and metric computation
